proposition.claim:
The primary reviewed source is the Aalto accepted manuscript of Liu, Peltola, and Wu, carrying arXiv:2108.04421v3, 31 May 2024. It has 58 physical PDF pages, including the repository cover; manuscript page \(p\) is physical page \(p+1\). The journal article is Annals of Probability 53 (2025), 23–78, DOI 10.1214/24-AOP1700 (https://doi.org/10.1214/24-AOP1700). A subsequently acquired, 56-page journal reprint hosted by BIMSA was checked at the corresponding statements and proof. This is a comparison of specified passages, not a certification that the two complete versions coincide.

The detailed inspection concerns the meander definition, the collision asymptotics in Theorems 1.1–1.2, the operations and proofs in Section 4.2, and the small-\(N\) formulas in Appendix B. The statements of Theorems 1.3–1.4 were read with their boundary regularity and approximation hypotheses. The full discrete-observable convergence proof, the entire hyperelliptic construction, and Appendix D were not independently verified.

Equation reference: eq:change. For \(N\) pairs, let \(\mathrm{LP}_N\) denote the noncrossing perfect matchings of \(1,\ldots,2N\). By (1.6), \(\mathcal M_{\alpha,\beta}=1\) precisely when the union of the two matchings forms one meander loop; otherwise it is zero. Equations (1.7) and (4.7) give \[
 \mathcal Z=\mathcal M^{-1}\mathcal F,\qquad \mathcal F_\beta=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathrm{LP}_N}
 \mathcal M_{\beta,\alpha}\mathcal Z_\alpha .\] For an adjacent pair \(j,j+1\), let \(r_j\) remove that pair when it is a link, and let \(t_j\) tie the two vertices, reconnect their former partners, and remove the newly formed pair when it was not a link. Remaining vertices are relabeled increasingly. These are respectively the paper’s \(\widehat\varrho_j\) and \(\widehat\wp_j\). Section 4.2 explicitly distinguishes the bijection \(r_j\) from the generally noninjective surjection \(t_j\) (manuscript p. 42; journal p. 64).

For each nonlinked alpha, lim h^(-1/4) Z_alpha = pi Z_tie_remove(alpha).
